# Every way an EraInfra Profile is deliberately not `ubuntu-latest`.
#
# `diff.sh` fingerprints a job on `ubuntu-latest` and on each Linux Profile and
# fails on every difference this file does not account for. So this file is the
# written record of the decisions: what we chose to be different about, and why.
# It did not exist before #82, which is why #80 -- a job capped at 8 CPUs while
# every interface it could read said 64 -- reached a production repository and
# was found by a user's test suite.
#
# Three directives, each of which MUST carry a `# reason`. An entry with no
# reason is a bug being hidden, so diff.sh treats a missing reason as a syntax
# error rather than a style preference.
#
#   allow <key-or-glob>            a difference in this key is intended
#   require <key>=<value>          this key must hold this value on EVERY leg
#   never-allow <key-or-glob>      `allow` may never name this key
#   pending <key>=<value> <date>   seen, owned by an issue, and time-boxed
#
# The differ warns about `allow` entries that matched no difference in a run.
# Most of those are rot and should go. A few are not: `runner_version` and
# `runner_action_archive_cache` are traceable to decisions here and merely
# happen to agree with GitHub's image this week, so they stay and the warning is
# expected. "Settled" means the reason no longer holds, not that the values
# matched once.
#
# `allow` and `pending` are different claims and the difference is the point.
# `allow` says "we meant this"; it is permanent and it requires the difference
# to be traceable to a decision recorded in this repository -- a flag in a
# provisioner, a line in the Dockerfile, an ADR, a documented product
# statement. `pending` says "we measured this, an issue owns it, and this line
# dies on that date". It pins the measured value, so a divergence that gets
# WORSE still fails, and it expires, so a question cannot be answered by
# forgetting it. Writing `allow` for something nobody has decided is the single
# way this file could become worse than useless.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two keys that are not negotiable
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# #80 is not "the CPU count differs". Of course it differs: a Worker is a
# different size from a hosted runner, and the entries further down say so. #80
# is that the count a job SEES disagreed with the count it was ALLOWED -- 64
# against a quota of 8 -- so every tool that autosizes (vitest, `make -j`,
# Go, the JVM, Python) oversubscribed by 8x. That gap is what the
# `*_matches_allowed` keys measure, and there is no fleet anywhere on which it
# is intended.
#
# They are handled twice on purpose:
#
#   `never-allow` stops the plausible entry. Someone reading a red job at 03:00
#   will reach for "our machines are bigger, allow it"; that reasoning is
#   correct for `cpu_visible_count` and fatal for this key, so the attempt is a
#   hard failure instead of a comment nobody reads.
#
#   `require` stops the silent one. This job is differential, and a
#   differential job cannot see a defect that both legs share: if hosted and
#   Profile were both misreporting their own size the two values would agree
#   and the diff would go green. These are asserted absolutely, per leg.
require cpu_visible_matches_allowed=yes  # a machine that reports more CPUs than its own quota allows lies to every build tool that autosizes; this is #80. Went green with #83's cpuset allocator (v0.2.0-rc.7), and became structural at the #17 cutover: a microVM guest has exactly its Profile's vCPUs and nothing else to misreport
require mem_visible_matches_allowed=yes  # #93, measured live on the Docker path: a job promised 2 GiB read 251 GiB from /proc/meminfo, a factor of 125, because a cgroup limit does not rewrite a kernel-global file. Fixed by #17's microVMs — the guest's /proc/meminfo IS its allowed memory, measured 1993 == 1993 (run 32330383534)
never-allow cpu_visible_matches_allowed  # the excusable difference is cpu_visible_nproc, which is allowed below; the agreement between what a job sees and what it may use is not
never-allow mem_visible_matches_allowed  # same shape as the CPU key: sizes may differ between legs, a machine disagreeing with itself may not
never-allow node_heap_within_allowed_mem  # Node sizes its default old space from total RAM, so a heap ceiling above the cgroup limit entitles a process to grow until the kernel kills it, and the OOM carries no stack
require workspace_free_meets_floor=yes  # 14 GiB is what GitHub documents a hosted Linux runner has free, so it is the floor a workflow written for `ubuntu-latest` is entitled to assume. Asserted per leg because the SIZES are allowed to differ below and a size comparison between two different machines answers a different question than "is there room to build"
require scratch_free_meets_floor=yes  # same floor, for RUNNER_TEMP: the directory actions/cache, setup-node and every `mktemp` in a workflow write to
require root_free_meets_floor=yes  # same floor, for the writable layer a `docker build` or an apt install lands in
never-allow workspace_free_meets_floor  # the room itself may differ; having enough of it may not
never-allow scratch_free_meets_floor  # same
never-allow root_free_meets_floor  # same
require sysctl_vm_max_map_count_meets_floor=yes  # 262144 is the documented floor Elasticsearch and OpenSearch refuse to start below, and the value hosted ships. The raw sysctl is allowed to differ below (the microVM guest boots at 1048576); this asserts per leg that no guest kernel or image change ever drops under the floor while the raw difference stays allowed
never-allow sysctl_vm_max_map_count_meets_floor  # the value may differ; clearing the floor may not

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The boundary itself
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow kernel_release  # a GitHub-hosted job runs on Azure's kernel; a Profile runs on the Worker's, or on the guest kernel deploy/provision-firecracker-host.sh pins. Both are pinned deliberately and neither tracks the other
allow virtualisation  # hosted is an Azure VM; the transitional Docker executor is a container and Firecracker is a microVM (ADR 0001)
allow lsm_profile  # a hosted job runs unconfined on Azure's kernel while the pinned 6.1 guest kernel reports `kernel` (run 32343905771); the LSM state is a property of the kernel each leg boots, and neither tracks the other. Docker's AppArmor profile, which this entry used to describe, died with the executor
allow dev_kvm  # GitHub enabled nested virtualisation on hosted Linux runners; the shared-kernel Docker executor exposes no device nodes at all, which #80's own evidence records as kvm=absent. Firecracker guests get real vCPUs instead (#17)
allow dev_fuse  # measured absent on the fleet, and the same decision as dev_kvm above: provision-docker.sh passes no --device and no --cap-add, and the daily smoke canary fails if a host mount ever appears
allow dev_net_tun  # same: no device node reaches an Attempt, which is what a shared-kernel boundary buys
allow dev_vhost_vsock  # same
allow dev_dri  # same; no GPU is exposed to any Profile today. The five device keys are listed in #96 too, so the record of what a shared-kernel Attempt does not get lives in one place

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Size. A Profile is a contract for a size, and it is not ubuntu-latest's
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each of these differs because a Profile carries `vcpus` and `memoryMiB`
# (convex/schema.ts) and a hosted runner carries whatever GitHub sells. None of
# them can express #80 on its own, which is exactly why the derived keys above
# exist and are not on this list.
allow cpu_visible_nproc  # a Profile's vcpus is not ubuntu-latest's 4
allow cpu_nproc_all  # the Worker host's core count, which no Profile promises to match
allow cpu_cpuinfo_count  # the Worker host's processor list, which /proc/cpuinfo reports whole and which no cpuset can narrow. The count differing between legs is a size difference; whether it agrees with nproc is a separate key and is not on this list
allow cpu_affinity_count  # the scheduler affinity mask a Profile hands the job
allow cpu_online_count  # the Worker host's online CPU set
allow cpu_cgroup_cpuset_count  # the cpuset width the executor allocates per Attempt
allow cpu_allowed_millicpu  # the resolved CPU ceiling, which is the Profile's vcpus on our side and the hosted VM's core count on GitHub's
allow cpu_node_available_parallelism  # what Node reports, which follows the affinity mask
allow mem_visible_mib  # the Worker host's RAM, which no Profile promises to match
allow mem_allowed_mib  # the Profile's memoryMiB against whatever the hosted runner ships
allow mem_node_totalmem_mib  # the same host RAM read through os.totalmem()
allow mem_swap_total_mib  # swap is a property of the Worker host, not of the Profile
allow node_heap_limit_mib  # V8 sizes its default old space from total RAM, so this moves with the number above it; whether it FITS is the assertion, and it is not on this list

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The three *_fstype keys left this section the same way the free-space
# buckets below did: the microVM guest writes to its own ext4 exactly as
# hosted's VM does, so the overlayfs difference died with the Docker executor
# and the entries covered nothing (run 32343905771).
#
# The three *_free_gib_pow2 keys had entries here until the first fleet run
# measured both legs into the same 64 GiB bucket. Nothing in this repository
# decides how much disk a Worker has, so an entry for it was speculation, and a
# speculative entry that matches nothing is exactly the rot this file cannot
# afford. If the buckets ever diverge the job goes red and somebody writes a
# real line with a measured reason, which is the outcome that was wanted.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The runner and its image
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow runner_environment  # `self-hosted` against `github-hosted` is the entire premise of the comparison
allow runner_version  # GitHub updates the hosted runner continuously; images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile pins actions/runner by version and SHA-256, and that pin is asserted there
allow runner_image_os  # ImageOS is set by GitHub's image provisioning and by nothing of ours
allow env_path  # the runner root and tool cache live at different paths in the two images. Whether a workflow can still FIND its tools is asserted by the tool_*_present keys, which are not on this list
allow user_groups  # the Image Release creates the runner account with exactly the docker and sudo groups; GitHub's image adds a dozen more for tooling we deliberately do not ship
allow user_gid  # images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile creates the runner account with `useradd --gid docker`, so its primary group is docker rather than a same-named user group. That is what lets a job reach the Docker group without a second membership lookup
allow toolcache_tools  # the Image Release is minimal on purpose (docs/research/blacksmith-runner-images.md): it carries the toolchain its Profiles were built for and is not advertised as GitHub-hosted-compatible
allow toolcache_node_versions  # same: one pinned Node, seeded so actions/setup-node resolves it without a download
allow tool_*_version  # our Image Release pins its toolchain and GitHub's floats, so version drift between the two is expected. A tool DISAPPEARING is not, and tool_*_present is not on this list -- that is the #48 bug class
allow docker_server_version  # the Image Release ships dockerd inside the guest and pins it — 29.1.3 against hosted's floating 28.0.4 (run 32343905771). Version drift between a pinned toolchain and a floating one, the same class as tool_*_version. That a daemon is reachable AT ALL now matches hosted — the old docker_daemon_reachable allow, which recorded the Docker executor refusing to mount a control socket, died with that executor
allow workspace_free_gib_pow2  # a Worker host's disk is not the one GitHub hands out, so the two legs land in different power-of-two buckets whenever they differ by more than a factor of two — measured 64 against 128 in one run and 64 against 64 in the run before it, with nothing having changed between them. The bucket exists so ONE machine reports the same number twice, not so two machines agree. What a job is actually entitled to is a floor, and that is required above rather than allowed here
allow scratch_free_gib_pow2  # same, for RUNNER_TEMP
allow dev_shm_size_mib  # both executors size /dev/shm at half the Profile's memory — provision-docker.sh via --shm-size (#90, shipped v0.2.0-rc.7), and the microVM guest's tmpfs default does the same arithmetic natively — while GitHub sizes it at half its runner's RAM, so the two differ exactly as the Profile's size differs from GitHub's 16 GiB. Measured: 1024 in the container (run 32102711080) and 997 in the guest (run 32330383534) on the 2 GiB rc-e2e Profile, against 7995 hosted. tmpfs size is a cap, not a reservation, so it grants no memory the limit did not already promise
allow root_free_gib_pow2  # same, for the container's writable layer
allow tool_pnpm_present  # the Image Release installs pnpm 11.21.0 (images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile) and GitHub's does not ship it at all, measured. A tool we have and they do not cannot break a workflow written for ubuntu-latest; the reverse can, which is why the rest of tool_*_present is not on this list

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deliberately NOT allowlisted, though it will fail
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A key belongs in this section when it is expected to go red and deliberately
# carries no directive at all, so that the red is read by a person rather than
# absorbed by a line in this file.
#
# It is empty today, and that is a state rather than an oversight. Two keys were
# held here and both have since graduated to entries above; what moved them is
# recorded because in each case it was a decision landing, not a mind changing.
#
#   cpu_nproc_matches_cpuinfo was prose here on the argument that allowlisting a
#   difference nobody has measured is how a record becomes a wish, then an
#   `allow` once the cpuset residue was measured on a production Worker
#   (nproc=8 against all 64 host processors in /proc/cpuinfo, cgroup v1,
#   Docker 28.1.1). The #17 cutover ended the story a third way: a microVM
#   guest's /proc/cpuinfo lists exactly its vCPUs, so the key agrees with
#   itself on both legs, the allow covered nothing (run 32343905771), and the
#   entry is gone. If the two ever disagree again, that is a machine lying
#   about its size — the exact regression this job exists to catch — and it
#   should go red unabsorbed.
#
#   dev_shm_size_mib went through all three states this file has, in order, and
#   the history is worth keeping: prose while 64 MiB was an unowned Docker
#   default nobody could call intended (#87), `pending dev_shm_size_mib=64`
#   once it was measured and #90 owned it, and `allow` above now that a fleet
#   running #90's fix has been measured -- v0.2.0-rc.7 on rc-e2e reads 1024,
#   half the Profile's 2 GiB, exactly what #90 chose (run 32102711080). The
#   pending entry did its last job on that same run: it refused to cover the
#   new value, because 1024 is a DIFFERENT divergence from the 64 it recorded.
#
# The two keys that once failed here are not in this section either, and
# deliberately: cpu_visible_matches_allowed and mem_visible_matches_allowed carry `require`
# and `never-allow` at the top of this file, which is stronger than silence --
# silence lets a difference pass unnoticed if it stops differing for the wrong
# reason, and `require` asserts it on every leg instead.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deliberately not fingerprinted
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recorded here because "why is X not checked" is the second question anyone
# asks this file, and because a dimension dropped without a note reads later
# like a dimension nobody thought of.
#
#   hostname, container id, IP addresses, uptime, PIDs, timestamps -- they move
#   between two runs on the SAME machine, so they cannot be diffed between two
#   different ones. Free space is fingerprinted as a power-of-two bucket for
#   the same reason -- and the bucket only makes ONE machine agree with itself,
#   so the buckets are allowed to differ between legs above and the assertion
#   that survives is the 14 GiB floor, which is `require`d per leg.
#
#   CPU model, vendor and instruction-set flags -- GitHub rotates hosted
#   hardware, so these differ from ubuntu-latest to ubuntu-latest. A dimension
#   that is not stable on the baseline cannot be conformance-checked against
#   it; a build that needs AVX-512 needs a Profile that promises it, which is a
#   Profile contract question and not this job's.
#
#   ImageVersion -- GitHub bumps it weekly. It would be an allowlisted key that
#   never fails, i.e. noise. The workflow prints it in the run summary instead.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recorded, owned, and time-boxed — NOT intended
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `pending` is not an allowlist entry. It says: this difference was measured, an
# issue owns it, and this line dies on that date. It fails if the divergence
# gets worse than the value recorded here, and it fails outright once the date
# passes, so it cannot quietly become permanent the way an `allow` with a
# hand-wave reason can.
#
# Everything below arrived in the FIRST run against a real Worker (run
# 32092987570): 103 keys identical, the differences above already accounted for,
# and these that nobody had written down. The rule that decides which list a
# difference lands on is at the top of this file: `allow` needs the difference
# to be traceable to a decision recorded in this repository. Nothing below is.
#
# NOT here, and deliberately: cpu_visible_matches_allowed and
# mem_visible_matches_allowed. Both were `no` on the fleet when this file was
# born -- #80 until v0.2.0-rc.7 carried #83's cpuset allocator, #93 until #17
# put every job in a microVM whose /proc IS its allowance -- and both are
# measured `yes` since run 32330383534. They stay `require`d above rather than
# retired: those two keys are the reason this job exists, the only
# continuously-checked statement that this platform tells a job the truth about
# its own size, and a regression in either goes red on its own leg.

# #94 and #95 are gone from this section the only way entries leave it: the
# defects died and a green run said so. #101 put the locale files, tzdata and
# the seven assumed tools in the image (run 32333001234 measured every one
# identical to hosted, and reported the pendings as covering nothing), and
# smoke.sh asserts each at image build so a regression fails before it ships.
# The same held for dev_shm_size_mib (#87/#90, now the `allow` above) and for
# swappiness, locked memory and core size, which the #17 cutover itself healed
# — the guest kernel's defaults match hosted where Docker's daemon did not.

# #96 measured the Docker daemon's defaults and the Worker host's kernel
# settings arriving through a gap nobody was looking at; the #17 cutover
# replaced them with the guest kernel's defaults, which are pinned but mostly
# memory-proportional — sized by the Profile's RAM rather than chosen. #112
# then set LANG and the inotify pair to hosted parity at the one place the
# guest actually builds a job's environment, each asserted at image build in
# smoke.sh. The pendings below are the remainder: guest kernel values still
# sized by RAM rather than chosen, owned by #110, plus #96's resolver shape
# and stack size, plus the open-files pair in transit (its entry tells that
# story). vm_max_map_count is the one graduate: a chosen value whose floor is
# `require`d absolutely above.
allow sysctl_vm_max_map_count  # the microVM guest boots at 1048576 against 262144 on hosted (run 32330383534; the Docker path measured the 5.4 host default 65530, which is why this was a pending). The value is chosen — the guest kernel and image are both pinned — and the floor that actually matters is asserted absolutely by `require sysctl_vm_max_map_count_meets_floor=yes` above, so this allow covers only the headroom, never a regression
pending sysctl_kernel_threads_max=15899 2026-11-16  # #110: memory-proportional kernel default on the 2 GiB guest against 127574 hosted; a bound a 2 GiB job rarely reaches, but it should be a decision at the guest-environment seam, not an artifact of guest RAM
pending sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces=7949 2026-11-16  # #110: memory-proportional kernel default on the 2 GiB guest against 63787 hosted; same decision, same seam
pending pids_cgroup_max=2384 2026-11-16  # #110: 2384 against 19151 hosted — another memory-proportional guest default. The old allow traced this to provision-docker.sh's --pids-limit 4096, a flag that no longer runs anywhere; what the guest grants today nobody chose, so it moves back to the state that says so
pending rlimit_max_open_files_soft=1048576 2026-11-16  # #110: #99 chose 65536 soft with 1048576 hard as raisable headroom, and the first run against it (32343905771) measured the headroom AS the soft limit — the runner is a .NET process and the runtime raises soft to hard at startup, handing every job the exact fd-range-walking stall the soft limit was chosen to prevent. The fix is LimitNOFILE=65536 on runner-center-guest.service, merged with this line; the digest that carries it kills this entry the way #87's died
pending rlimit_max_open_files_hard=1048576 2026-11-16  # #110: as above — same unit line, same fix, same death
pending rlimit_max_processes_soft=7949 2026-11-16  # #110: the Docker path measured unlimited — no blast-radius bound at all; the guest's memory-proportional 7949 against 63787 hosted is at least A bound, but a fork-heavy suite can reach it. Set it deliberately at the #110 seam
pending rlimit_max_processes_hard=7949 2026-11-16  # #110: as above, hard limit
pending rlimit_max_stack_size_soft=8388608 2026-11-16  # #96: 8 MiB against 16 MiB on hosted; deeply recursive builds and some parsers notice
pending rlimit_max_pending_signals_soft=7949 2026-11-16  # #110: memory-proportional guest default against 63787 hosted, same decision as max_processes, same seam
pending rlimit_max_pending_signals_hard=7949 2026-11-16  # #110: as above, hard limit
pending net_ipv6_disabled=unavailable 2026-11-16  # #110: the guest boots with ipv6.disable=1 (the job network policy is v4-only), so /proc/sys/net/ipv6 does not exist, while hosted has IPv6 up. Anything binding or dialing ::1 behaves differently. Either enable v6 in the guest with the policy extended to cover it, or freeze this divergence with a documented reason — a decision, not a leftover
allow sysctl_kernel_unprivileged_userns_clone  # a Debian-specific knob that does not exist on the vanilla 6.1 guest kernel (measured unavailable against 1 hosted, run 32330383534). The capability it gates is on by default there — sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces measures non-zero in the same run — so the absent knob is a kernel-flavor difference, not a capability difference
pending dns_nameserver_count=2 2026-11-16  # #96: the resolver shape a container inherits rather than one anyone picked. All four dns_resolves_* probes are identical and green on both legs; short-name resolution and edns0 retry behaviour are what differ
pending dns_nameserver_loopback=no 2026-11-16  # #96: the resolver shape a container inherits rather than one anyone picked. All four dns_resolves_* probes are identical and green on both legs; short-name resolution and edns0 retry behaviour are what differ
pending dns_options=unavailable 2026-11-16  # #96: the resolver shape a container inherits rather than one anyone picked. All four dns_resolves_* probes are identical and green on both legs; short-name resolution and edns0 retry behaviour are what differ
pending dns_search_domain_count=0 2026-11-16  # #96: the resolver shape a container inherits rather than one anyone picked. All four dns_resolves_* probes are identical and green on both legs; short-name resolution and edns0 retry behaviour are what differ
